newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican Cetes rate ends off, assuaged by US T-bond.
newsitem.headline: Mexican Cetes rate ends off, assuaged by US T-bond.

text.p: The Mexican overnight Cetes rate closed 65 basis points lower at 23.15 percent as domestic and foreign buyers entered the market after U.S. Treasuries had a mild response to solid August jobs data, traders said.

"Employment was within expectations and reduced jitters among investors who wished to take advantage of current rates, especially if you bear in mind that rates are expected to fall at next week's primary auction," a trader said.
Some dealers are expecting the benchmark 28-day Cetes rate to fall by over 150 basis points from its current 25.47 percent at next week's private auction.
In the term market, government 28-day and 91-day paper closed 80 and 60 basis points down at 24 and 28 percent, respectively.
Traders confirmed that foreign investors entering the Mexican markets firmed up the benchmark 48-hour spot peso by 5.5 centavos to 7.5560/7.5600.

Banco de Mexico earlier relieved liquidity shortfalls by injecting 4.399 billion pesos via three credit auctions, where the lowest assignment rate was 24.66 percent, compared to 25.59 percent on Thursday.
Overnight bank paper meanwhile closed 80 basis points down at 24.50 percent.
Credits totalling 7.451 billion pesos fall due on Monday and will put pressure on liquidity.
